subject.title: Write tool lacks append mode — isolated cron sessions destroy shared files

question: Should OpenClaw accept `append?: boolean` on the existing `write` tool as the permanent append contract for ordinary agent, cron, and monitor workflows, or require a different append API before closing this issue?
rationale: The failure is source-reproducible, but the remaining fix becomes a public model-facing and extension-observable tool contract that automation should not approve without maintainer intent.

options.title: Accept append on write
options.body: Land the linked implementation after conflict resolution and maintainer review, keeping overwrite as the default and using `append: true` for safe accumulation.

options.title: Choose a different append contract
options.body: Ask for a replacement shape such as `mode: "append"` or a dedicated append tool before merging any public API.

options.title: Defer the code change
options.body: Keep the issue open and rely on backup, prompt, or shell-redirect workarounds, accepting that ordinary write calls can still truncate shared files.

recommendation.title: Accept append on write
recommendation.body: Land the linked implementation after conflict resolution and maintainer review, keeping overwrite as the default and using `append: true` for safe accumulation.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a shared agent-runtime/tool-contract product decision, and steipete is both listed as project decision owner and the strongest recent code-routing signal for the current write-tool surface.
